title: RM Attitude as the Sixth Dramatistic Term
aligns_with: gm-pentad-operationalization-manual.md (Section A forward_reference_to_rhetoric_of_motives_attitude; Section E Rhetoric-Attitude column)
ig-pim-operationalization-manual.md (Section A.5 AFFECTIVE -> Layer-B target = ATTITUDE)

section_A_operational_definition.definition: Attitude = the dispositional term naming an INCIPIENT ACT — a leaning/inclination/orientation toward action not yet (or not necessarily) carried into overt conduct; the suspended/rehearsal mode mediating between potency (dynamis) and full act (energeia).
section_A_operational_definition.core_quote_paraphrase: rhetorical language is inducement to action OR to attitude, attitude being an incipient act (RM-01 p.42)
section_A_operational_definition.question_answered: in what disposition / with what orientation was (or would) the act be done?

two_senses.incipient_act: attitude as the BEGINNING of an act; arrow points toward action (RM-02 pp.50-51; Mead/Richards seeds)
two_senses.suspended_act: attitude as a HELD orientation that may never be consummated; arrow arrested (Kierkegaard RM-06 p.251; mystic 'status nascendi' RM-07 pp.331-332)
two_senses.unity: two faces of one term: an act in potentia whose actualization is incipient and may be perpetually suspended — the 'suspended/incipient/symbolic-rehearsal mode' the Grammar manual forecast.

boundary_criteria: not yet overt conduct (if completed external act -> code Act, RM-02 pp.50-51)
distinct from Purpose (Purpose = end-toward-which; Attitude = disposition-with-which; one purpose, many attitudes)
can be the terminal target of rhetoric (lyric/poetic aim at attitude only; persuasion-to-attitude more general than persuasion-to-action, T3)

rhetoric_of_motives.anchor: Avarice = scenic word 'property' translated into agent's attitude/incipient act

rhetoric_of_motives.role: attitude INTERNAL to consubstantiality — hinge to bridge

rhetoric_of_motives.anchor: persuasion to attitude vs persuasion to action; attitude as leaning/inclination
rhetoric_of_motives.role: persuasion-to-attitude is the more general target

rhetoric_of_motives.anchor: censorial appellative as tonal gesture; Bentham 'incipient act'; headlines as postures
rhetoric_of_motives.role: attitude as orientation that disposes without completing argument

rhetoric_of_motives.anchor: ultimate vocabulary organizes 'one's attitude toward the struggles of politics' (Mr So-and-so -> 'the Proletarian')
rhetoric_of_motives.role: attitudinal-purpose realignment prior to specific act

rhetoric_of_motives.anchor: perpetual courtship: 'renunciation and advance fused in one attitude'
rhetoric_of_motives.role: paradigm of the SUSPENDED-act sense (Burke's own formulation)
attitude as incipient-act whose full enactment is the climbing
attitude at its most concentrated; suspended-act at the limit (pure incipience)
systematic incipience held against drive to acquisition

grammar_cross_refs_1962_lineage.anchor: symbolic action as realm of incipient/attitudinal
Burke NAMES Attitude as the 6th term
grammar_cross_refs_1962_lineage.role: load-bearing self-citation: Attitude is Burke's own later addition
RM p.42 consolidates these; attitude mediates potency<->energeia

section_C_modifies_five_grammar_terms.principle: Attitude is a DISPOSITIONAL MODIFIER (the disposition-with-which) transverse to the pentad, not a sixth box. Grammar manual placed it as a COLUMN across all five terms; this populates that column with burke-direct content.

modifiers.attitude_modifier: incipient-act sub-term / symbolic-rehearsal spectrum; same doing in different attitudes; some 'acts' are attitudes literally enacted
modifiers.calleja_link: readiness-to-move; theorycrafting/rehearsed play (Kinesthetic readiness; Ludic strategy-rehearsal)

modifiers.attitude_modifier: attitudinal-scene: situation-as-already-evaluated; rhetorical scene of address pre-loaded with evaluative tone
modifiers.calleja_link: gameworld encountered as already affectively coloured (atmospherics-as-affect; 'I want to live there')

modifiers.attitude_modifier: agent's dispositional stance / identification-disposition; shared attitudes make agents consubstantial; stance toward co-agents = incipient act of identification
rhetorical-instrumentality of address; means deployed IN an attitude; censorial appellative as tonal gesture
modifiers.calleja_link: attitudinal coloring of control/rule-use; standoffish element of skilled performance (Kinesthetic/Ludic, Performative)

modifiers.attitude_modifier: attitudinal-purpose: the end held in a disposition; ultimate vocabulary realigns attitude; pure persuasion = purpose in perpetual standoffishness
modifiers.calleja_link: same goal in different registers (completionist vs competitive vs ironic-meta) (Ludic + Narrative + Affective)

section_C_modifies_five_grammar_terms.modifier_not_box: pentad answers what/where/who/how/why; Attitude answers a transverse SIXTH question 'in what disposition?' that can be asked of any of the five — hence a column, not a row.

argument: 1. consubstantiality is partly constituted by shared attitudes (RM-01 p.21, burke-direct)
2. attitude is an incipient act (RM-01 p.42, burke-direct)
3. therefore a player's disposition toward avatar/guild/gameworld is an incipient act of identification (anticipatory-projection)
section_D_hinge_identification_and_affec.role: Attitude is the dispositional hinge linking identification (master term -> Shared/Incorporation) to affect (felt register -> Affective).
section_D_hinge_identification_and_affec.two_pipeline_convergence: Calleja independently assigns AFFECTIVE the Layer-B target 'ATTITUDE (Burke's later sixth term)' (ig-pim A.5, E.1). Burke's 6th term and Calleja's Affective Layer-B target converge from opposite directions — evidence the mapping is structural.

section_E_player_attitude_register.note: All anticipatory-projection. Each register = a sustained dispositional stance (incipient/suspended act) toward the gameworld; foregrounds Calleja AFFECTIVE; recruits a secondary dimension + pentad emphasis. Registers are NOT mutually exclusive (a player oscillates).

registers.burke_grounding: hierarchy / the kill / 'proving opposites'; invidious distinction (RM-04; RM-07 pp.252-266)
registers.disposition: agonistic striving up the rank-hierarchy; incipient act of out-imitating/overcoming co-agents

registers.burke_grounding: perpetual courtship; pure persuasion self-interference; Keats-Urn single-need-forever-courted (RM-06 p.251; RM-07 pp.269-275)
registers.disposition: suspended-act: engagement sustained by impossibility of final acquisition; approach prized over attainment

registers.burke_grounding: range of mountings (kinesthetic/spatial/anagogic); imaging of transformation; scene-as-already-evaluated (RM-07 pp.301-313; RM-00; RM-01 p.24)
registers.disposition: dwelling-toward / ascending-through the scene; incipient act of inhabiting place as already-evaluated

registers.burke_grounding: ultimate identification; reverence/mystery/'glory' as addressed motive; martyrdom-as-witness (RM-07 pp.328-333; RM-06 pp.222-233)
registers.disposition: reverent self-subordination to the gameworld's universal order / hierarchic principle; identification toward the absolute

registers.burke_grounding: comic primness; humble/classic irony; 'demons of Rhetoric'/cunning identification; standoffishness (RM-04 comic-primness; RM-01 pp.35-37; RM-07 pp.269-271)
registers.disposition: suspended-act: detached, self-aware engagement — playing WITH the game's rhetoric rather than wholly WITHIN it (speedrun/meta-gaming)

register_notes: not mutually exclusive; a single act can be performed in more than one register (Attitude-as-modifier)
elation/accidie arc (RM-07 pp.313-318) cuts across all five: each has a sustained ('elation') and disrupted ('accidie') phase

ironic-meta connects to Grammar Section-D irony battery Q40 (humble irony = consubstantiality with the toxic optimizer; the analyst's and the player's attitude are the same Burkean term at two levels)

how_attitude_completes_the_six_term_axis.attitude_question: transverse sixth = 'in what disposition?' (askable of any of the five)
completion_points: closes the potency->act arc (incipient/suspended mode mediating dynamis and energeia)
is internal to consubstantiality (shared attitudes make agents consubstantial, p.21) -> hinge of the keystone bridge
is the meeting-point of the two pipelines (Burke's 6th term = Calleja's Affective Layer-B target)
supplies the player-disposition typology grounding Affective involvement
how_attitude_completes_the_six_term_axis.result: five questions of PLACEMENT + one of DISPOSITION = the complete six-term apparatus the Burke x Calleja integration deploys.
